title: MCMC & Posterior Sampling
interviewAnswer: MCMC constructs a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is the posterior, letting us approximate expectations when closed-form inference is unavailable. Diagnostics are essential because samples can be correlated or chains may not mix.
keyPoints: Burn-in/warmup is not a substitute for convergence diagnostics.
Check multiple chains, R-hat and effective sample size.
Posterior samples enable arbitrary derived quantities.
why: MCMC & Posterior Sampling appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Burn-in/warmup is not a substitute for convergence diagnostics.
deepDive: MCMC constructs a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is the posterior, letting us approximate expectations when closed-form inference is unavailable. Diagnostics are essential because samples can be correlated or chains may not mix. Check multiple chains, R-hat and effective sample size. Posterior samples enable arbitrary derived quantities. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Fit a hierarchical conversion model and use posterior draws to estimate probability one segment outperforms another.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does MCMC & Posterior Sampling make?
How would you validate or debug MCMC & Posterior Sampling in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
